title: Parents' names and the Barbados Callender family
summary: He names his parents, explains the Bajan Sylvester name, and tells of Callender family reunions and ancestors who left Scotland for the Caribbean.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: about. About your mother and your father, can we have their names on their tape?

My mother's maiden name was Hattie Lee Spense, and my father's name was George Lawrence Callender. So although my name is George Sylvester Callender... I'm a junior, but I guess that wouldn't be approved on me because my middle name is different than my father's. But anyhow, they used to call me George Junior Callender. And I can remember when I first went to school and my father took me, and said, "George Callender, Junior," and I said, "no, my name is George Junior Callender." I finally figured it out that my name was George Callender, Junior, with Sylvester in the middle.
When you mentioned the Sylvester in the beginning, that was from the Bajan?

Yes, the Sylvester part is the Bajan, or Barbados. That's a popular name in Barbados. And incidentally, we were in Barbados a few years ago. It's a small island, 21 miles long and 14 miles wide at the largest part. And in the phone book, Callender could compare to Smith here; it's mostly Callenders in Barbados.
Yes. And we have an historian, as a matter of fact, a family historian. On Labor Day the Callender

clan meets in Lunenberg(?), Massachusetts. My first cousin on my father's side has this family meeting every year, and Callenders from all over the country and Barbados get together. I haven't been yet, because I've been a little too busy on Labor Days to go. But there's another meeting this year.

And what I had started to say is that our family traces back to 1700, when five brothers, for whatever reason, had to leave Scotland, and they settled in the Caribbean, and married Indian women, African women and mulatto women and all sorts of women. I guess that's why you'd call me a real mongrel. Here I am, whatever color I am, I have freckles...
...and red hair. And it all dates back to some Callender in Scotland.
You didn't know that, did you.
I didn't know that. No, I didn't know. I didn't know that Callender was a Bajan name. I didn't know about all the Callenders in Barbados.
